title: Compat-mode sunset and regression lab for streaming, tool-calls, and structured outputs
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: We are changing default behavior for structured-output parsing, tool/function calling handshake semantics, and streaming token termination in api-v2. These changes improve safety and reduce ambiguous parsing but will break some existing clients that relied on the old heuristics. Goal: define a short, time-boxed compatibility mode (compat_v1), a clear deprecation and sunset timeline, a migration guide for customers and SDKs, and an automated regression lab to validate backward compatibility across representative workloads. This ticket coordinates PM work: finalize timelines, write migration docs, define acceptance metrics, and own the customer communication plan. Engineering tickets will implement flags, test harness, and telemetry gating. Design will review error messaging and deprecation notices in the Console and SDKs.
acceptance_criteria: Compat flag (compat_v1) exists and is honored by hosted API and Redwood SDKs
Migration doc published with examples for streaming, tool-calls, and structured outputs (examples for Node, Python)
Regression lab exists and runs nightly against a representative corpus with automated diffing
Performance and SLO metrics show <1% increase in median latency when compat_v1 is enabled
Customer opt-in telemetry and opt-out paths instrumented; can enumerate which customers use compat_v1
Sunset date communicated to affected customers at least 30 days before default flip
updates: 2026-03-01: Ticket created after cross-functional kickoff. PM readout to Eng/Design/Reliability. Assigned to Tomas Rivera.

2026-03-04: Eng proposed two implementation options for streaming termination: (A) preserve old EOS heuristics behind compat_v1; (B) translate old heuristics to a deterministic post-processing step. Eng prefers (A) for faster rollout; cost estimate higher. Action: prototype (A) and evaluate tail-latency impact.
2026-03-06: Design provided copy for deprecation banners in Console and SDK warnings. UX recommended explicit example links next to banners.
2026-03-08: Reliability flagged potential capacity impact when compat_v1 is used with legacy batching; added ENG-3420 to dependencies to track autoscaler tweaks.
2026-03-10: Migration guide draft uploaded to Confluence (link below). PM requested more end-to-end examples for tool-call error recovery.
2026-03-12: Regression harness spec agreed in sync: nightly runs, seed corpus of 3k prompts, schema-aware diffs, and failure triage flow. Eng to add flaky test suppression rules.

2026-03-14: PM reviewed prototype results. Median latency cost with compat_v1: +0.7% on p3-small pools. Decided to proceed with compat_v1 behind behavior flag and start email outreach to Top-100 users in trial cohort.
decision_log: Prefer additive compatibility flag (compat_v1) rather than in-place heuristics translation to minimize risk to default path.
Sunset approach: 90-day opt-in, 30-day pre-flip notice, final removal 120 days after first public announcement unless critical customers request extension.
Regressions threshold: nightly lab failure rate >0.5% triggers hold and rollback of default flip in that release window.
SDKs will expose explicit parameter in client constructors and throw an actionable error when legacy semantics cannot be satisfied.
We will not block the API default change on non-critical telemetry gaps; instead create a follow-up to add per-customer flags in Dedicated and Private (ENG-3491).
test_plan: Nightly regression lab: run 3k representative prompts covering streaming, tool-call sequences, nested structured outputs; produce diffs per model and per seq-length bucket.
E2E tests: Node and Python SDK examples that validate function calling handshake and structured schema evolution (happy path + schema-mismatch recovery).
Fuzz tests: random token stream truncations and delayed tool-responses to validate intermediary state handling.
Canary suite: small percentage of traffic (1%) routed to default-new behavior with fast rollback hook; monitor error-rate, latency, and structured-output schema failures.
Compatibility matrix tests: combinations of client SDK versions x server flags x model families to ensure no silent behavioral regressions.
Manual exploratory sessions with top-5 customers in trial cohort, capture edge cases and add to corpus for continuous testing.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (now): Feature flag behind internal toggle; prototype validated on staging clusters.
Phase 1 (2 weeks): Publish migration guide + SDK examples; expose compat_v1 as opt-in parameter in hosted API and SDKs; start nightly regression lab.
Phase 2 (6 weeks): Invite Top-100 customers to opt-in trial; run canary traffic to measure real-world regressions; collect feedback and patch SDKs.
Phase 3 (12 weeks): Default behavior flip in hosted API for new customers and SDKs; compat_v1 remains available for existing customers for 90 days.
Phase 4 (post-flip): 30-day notice emails and Console banners before removing compat_v1; final removal after addressing any critical customer requests.
notes_for_engineering: Ensure compat flag is honored in Dedicated and Private control plane; if not possible, document exact limitations.
Add granular telemetry: per-request flag usage, model family, SDK version, and streaming termination code path.
Avoid increasing default tail-latency beyond SLO; if unavoidable, add fallback policy to bypass legacy heuristics after timeout.
customer_communication: Email template drafted and staged for Top-100 outreach (Confluence link above).
Console banner with link to migration guide to be shown to customers using streaming or tool-calls.
Support playbook for Tier 1 to triage migration issues and escalate to Eng on rollback requests.
